comments.author: @zoey-c9q2c
comments.text: It's nonsense to imagine that the US government cannot become insolvent due to it owing bills in it's own printable currency. All it takes is for creditors to longer believe to raise the price of the credit and supress the value of the currency. All it takes for the currency to be effectively without value, thereby ending US solvency, is a critical mass of investors believing that the US either can't or won't produce as much value as other available investments. That is, if the US does not continue to increase value, it cannot continue to increase debt because creditors would rather lend to organizations that can continue to increase value. There are already many US and global firms that diversify against the US and offer funds that specifically do not include US government or business lending. Check out VXUS, VEU, and IXUS for example. They're offering ~2.5% dividends and are each up 10% or more this year with performance similar to russel/sp/nsdq meaning that these exUS funds are currently doing just as well or better than US indices meaning that an investor worried about US viability could rest easy in skipping it.
